items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: The first time I heard King Oliver, at a parade at the Central Rock Cemetery... I remember King Oliver, tall with his horn.

ctx.x: did you recognize any of the guys later? Oh, later on I got to know them like, for instance, like

Black Nolan, Buckeye Wilford. What did they play? They played piano. All these were piano players? They played the blues, yeah, piano players. Black Nolan, Buckeye Wilford. Yeah, they were always welcome. Shine, regular hunky-tunk piano players. First time I heard what it's called now Boogie Woogie. The first time I heard that beat, my little uncle said, look at that guy playing them horses. He used to call it the horses in New Orleans. It wasn't Boogie Woogie, it was horses, because it sounded like a horse's…
Go ahead, it's ready Danny on the second reel.
Did you know Papa Joe Oliver?
Yes, I knew Joe Oliver. Do you think, I mean, some people,

some people have indicated that he really wanted Louis to stay with him in Chicago when Louis left and went to New York, and that I think Lil Armstrong, his wife, his second wife, sort of had an influence on his leaving the band. Do you think there was any bitterness on Joe's part when Louis left to go to Chicago?

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: King Oliver played in that band. ... I saw my grandfather marching. ... See King Oliver. In those days we’d have maybe six or seven guys following right within hearing distance... to listen to King Oliver blow

ctx.x: Earlier. Before my time. Baquet was in that band. All them greats had been through that band. Papa Celestin. What’s his name? Bad man. Great trumpet player. His name phased out, because he was very unpopular, because he had a temper. King Oliver played in that band. Bunk Johnson played in that band. Before that Alcibiades Jeanjacque, he played in that band. He was a virtuoso trumpet player. Cornet player. Played in the circuses. He was supposed to go with Ringling Bros. in Ringling Bros.’s band, but they weren’t…

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: he was with King Oliver's band... King Oliver, none of them was playing that shit then.

ctx.x: You know, he bought my first banjo for me, because he was with King Oliver's band. Well...
